reviews.title: Serious Privacy Concern
reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed and upset with my recent experience using Snapchat.

When I opened the application, my face appeared on the camera screen. I generally dislike this feature and do not wish to take pictures of myself every time I open Snapchat.

Unfortunately, while interacting with the screen, the camera captured a picture and it was immediately posted without me realising what had happened.

What concerns me most is that Snapchat did not provide any confirmation message, warning, or “Are you sure you want to post this?” notification before publishing the picture.

I never intended to take this photograph, let alone share it with my friends. Something so personal should never be published without a clear and conscious action from the user.

The experience caused me significant embarrassment and distress. I even felt compelled to remove several friends from my Snapchat account because of what happened.

I should not have to worry that simply opening an application could result in an unwanted photograph of myself being shared with other people.

I strongly believe Snapchat needs to reconsider this design. At the very least, users should have:

1. An option to disable the camera opening automatically.
2. A clear confirmation before any photograph or content is published.
3. Better protection against accidental captures and posts.
4. Greater control over personal privacy.

I would appreciate it if this feedback were taken seriously and escalated to the relevant product

Snapchat has genuinely crossed a line with this latest update‼️‼️. The decision to make users pay to access their own Memories is not only disappointing, it feels like a complete disregard for the community that built the platform in the first place. These are our photos, our videos, and our personal moments not premium features that should be locked behind a subscription.

What makes this even worse is how unnecessary and tone-deaf the change is. People have been asking for better camera quality, fewer bugs, and a cleaner interface. Instead, Snapchat chose to monetize the one feature that kept many of us loyal to the app. The reaction speaks for itself: users everywhere are frustrated, confused, and honestly insulted.

It feels less like an update and more like Snapchat is holding our memories hostage unless we pay up. That’s not innovation — it’s exploitation. And the truth is, people are already talking about leaving. No one is going to stay on an app that punishes its long-time users and puts profit over trust.

If Snapchat refuses to listen and continues down this path, they’re going to lose a huge portion of their user base. We’re not paying for something that has been free for years, and we’re not going to support an app that treats its community like a revenue machine instead of actual people‼️.

Snapchat needs to fix this or they need to be ready to watch users walk away.⚠️⚠️⚠️

Snapchat has genuinely crossed a line with this latest update!! !!. The decision to make users pay to access their own Memories is not only disappointing, it feels like a complete disregard for the community that built the platform in the first place. What makes this even worse is how unnecessary and tone-deaf the change is. People have been asking for better camera quality, fewer bugs, and a cleaner interface. Instead, Snapchat chose to monetize the one feature that kept many of us loyal to the app. The reaction speaks for itself: users everywhere are frustrated, confused, and honestly insulted.
It feels less like an update and more like Snapchat is holding our memories hostage unless we pay up.
That's not innovation - it's exploitation. And the truth is, people are already talking about leaving. No one is going to stay on an app that punishes its long-time users and puts profit over trust.
If Snapchat refuses to listen and continues down this path, they're going to lose a huge portion of their user base. We're not paying for something that has been free for years, and we're not going to support an app that treats its community like a revenue machine instead of actual people?!!
Snapchat needs to fix this or they need to be ready to watch users walk away!..

reviews.text:
Let’s be very clear about what’s happening here: Snapchat has decided that personal memories are a monetisation opportunity. Not optional perks. Not luxury add ons. Core human experiences locked behind a paywall.

Forcing users to pay to retain access to their own memories is not innovation. It’s not “storage management.” It’s predatory design, deliberately engineered to exploit emotional attachment and sunk cost. You know users cannot simply “let go” of memories. You know they will pay out of pressure, not desire. And you are counting on that.

This is the kind of decision that reveals a company’s values in full daylight. When profit is prioritised over basic human decency, when coercion is disguised as a subscription model, when the message becomes “pay us or lose something personal” that’s not a tech company anymore. That’s extraction.

What makes this especially disturbing is the total lack of choice or dignity given to users. No meaningful export. No respectful alternatives. Just a funnel that leads to payment or loss. That is not user centric design that is emotional leverage.

People are not data limits. Memories are not expendable files. And users should not have to financially negotiate with an app to keep what is already theirs.

This behaviour deserves backlash, mass uninstalls, and public scrutiny. Because once companies learn they can monetise something this intimate, there is no line they won’t cross next

reviews.title: MEMORY STORAGE
reviews.text:
I’ve been a loyal Snapchat user since 2018, and honestly this new storage update is beyond disappointing — it’s frustrating, greedy, and completely out of touch with users who’ve supported this app for YEARS.

Snapchat used to be simple, fun, and reliable. Now it feels like every update just finds a new way to take away basic features and push users into paying more. The new storage system is confusing, restrictive, and honestly feels like a slap in the face to long-term users who trusted this app with their memories.

Snapchat is literally built around memories — snaps, videos, moments we can’t get back. Suddenly limiting storage or locking access behind updates without proper warning is unacceptable. No clear communication, no proper options, just “deal with it.” That’s not how you treat a loyal user base. The app already drains battery, crashes, and lags — and now we’re expected to accept storage restrictions too?
Loyal users should not feel punished for using the app the way it was intended.

If this is the direction Snapchat is going, then it’s extremely disappointing. Please listen to your users, revert or seriously improve this storage update, and stop prioritizing monetization over user experience.

Long-time users deserve better.

reviews.title: Completely Greedy and Selfish
reviews.text: It honestly feels greedy and selfish that Snapchat puts a price on memory space, because memories aren’t just files taking up storage, they’re pieces of real life that you don’t get back once they’re gone. I’ve used Snapchat for years to quietly document the moments that matter most to me, like watching my niece grow up one video and picture at a time, capturing her laugh, her first words, the small moments that don’t seem important until you realize how fast time moves. Those memories weren’t meant to be locked behind a paywall. Some of the most meaningful things in my memories aren’t even about the future, but about holding onto the past, especially the videos and photos of my dad. He’s gone now, and those clips are some of the few pieces of him I still have. Hearing his voice, seeing his face, watching moments that will never happen again…that isn’t “extra storage,” that’s grief, love, and connection. Being asked to pay just to keep those moments feels cruel, like a company profiting off people’s attachment to their own lives. Memories shouldn’t be treated like a luxury or an upgrade, especially when they hold the faces and voices of people you can never get back. It feels wrong that something so personal, so human, can be reduced to a subscription, as if the value of my relationships and my loss can be measured by how much I’m willing to spend each month.

Je suis profondément dégoûtée par la dernière mise à jour de Snapchat. Comment est-ce possible qu’on doive maintenant payer pour conserver nos souvenirs dans les “Memories” ? 😡 Jusqu’à aujourd’hui, on a pu sauvegarder des photos et des vidéos personnelles, parfois des souvenirs qui comptent, gratuitement ! Et là, d’un coup, on nous impose une limite — 5 Go — et si tu dépasses, c’est abonnement payant ou adieu tes souvenirs…  ￼
C’est un scandale : notre passé numérique, nos souvenirs personnels, ne devraient pas devenir une marchandise. Beaucoup ont utilisé Snapchat pendant des années, enregistré des centaines ou milliers de photos/vidéos — des moments de vie, des amis, des événements — et maintenant l’appareil se vend comme un coffre payant. Ce n’est pas juste.  ￼En plus, le changement est fait de façon sournoise : l’application a laissé croire pendant des années que l’option était gratuite et illimitée. Et soudain, on nous demande de payer ou de tout perdre. Ça s’appelle de l’abus, de l’exploitation pure des utilisateurs fidèles.
C’est un choix de design business pour Snapchat, mais du point de vue utilisateur c’est immoral. Ils transforment des souvenirs, parfois irremplaçables, en rente. Pour ma part, c’est clair : je n’accepte pas de payer pour un truc qui m’a été vendu gratuit — je trouve ça honteux. 😤

Chaque photo, chaque vidéo, chaque fragment de notre histoire personnelle est désormais otage d’une cupidité sans bornes. On pourrait presque sentir l’arrogance des concepteurs, assis dans leurs bureaux climatisés, riant de notre frustration, transformant notre nostalgie en marchandise comme un marché sordide. C’est une audace qui dépasse l’entendement : on se fait spolier de notre mémoire par des gens qui ne comprennent rien à la valeur d’un souvenir, qui réduisent nos vies à des chiffres sur un écran. La rage monte naturellement, parce que ce n’est pas seulement un bug ou une maladresse : c’est un coup de poignard dans le dos de tous les utilisateurs, une trahison qui brûle plus fort que n’importe quel dysfonctionnement technique. Leur logique est un labyrinthe pervers, leur cupidité un feu dévorant, et nous, pauvres utilisateurs, sommes coincés dans ce brasier de frustration, impuissants, indignés, presque humiliés par l’audace grotesque de cette décision. En bref, cette mise à jour n’est pas juste catastrophique : elle est scandaleusement insolente, et elle restera comme une tache noire dans l’histoire de cette application que nous avons jadis aimée.

reviews.title: Disappointing, Greedy, and Exploitative

Photos from 2014 — my memories, my life — and suddenly I’m told they may be erased?
What am I supposed to do with all these photos? Where am I supposed to move them? Why should users suffer because of your poor and greedy business decisions?

This is not an improvement or a better user experience. This is emotional pressure and financial manipulation, using people’s memories to extract money. Instead of respecting long-time users, Snapchat traps them in an unfair situation:
Pay… or lose your memories.

This decision is unethical, disrespectful, and deeply disappointing.
Snapchat used to be about capturing moments, but now it feels like a platform built on pressure and exploitation. If this continues, many users will permanently lose trust in this app.

reviews.title: Storage update😡
reviews.text:
I’m 20 years old and I’ve had Snapchat since I was 13. For seven years, the main and honestly the only reason I’ve stayed on this app is for the Memories. They hold irreplaceable photos and videos from my childhood and teenage years. Now, Snapchat is putting those same memories behind a paywall, something that was always free before, and that’s incredibly disappointing.

A huge portion of Snapchat’s user base is now in adulthood, and many of us only use the app as long term storage for personal memories. Forcing people to pay just to keep access to their own history feels greedy and unfair. It’s especially upsetting knowing that users now feel pressured to either pay for storage out of fear of losing everything, or go through the stressful process of transferring years of memories to iCloud or another device just so they can delete the app.

What started off as a fun app has now become a money grab. I can assure you there are plenty of other apps that can be used to communicate with friends and offer the same things Snapchat does. This upgrade has completely changed that. That’s exactly why I’m leaving. I refuse to pay for something that was free for years and that I trusted Snapchat to protect. This update has completely changed how I see the company, and not in a good way. What used to feel like a fun, meaningful app now feels like a cash grab at the expense of loyal users.

reviews.title: Memories

For so many of us, Snapchat has been the place where our whole teenage years are stored birthdays, friendships, holidays, inside jokes, all of it. These aren’t just photos; they’re the only record we have of some of the most important moments in our lives and we can’t even keep them anymore? It’s really upset me and many people i know. 

I honestly love the app and use it every day, but paying just to view Memories that I already saved feels unfair and honestly a bit upsetting. A lot of us are still in school, don’t have spare money, and rely on Snapchat because it’s always been free to access what we’ve already created. I don’t think this is fair as it’s been most people’s main source of taking photos and now it seems as though you’re just looking for the money and not our support. I know that if this isn’t able to change many people are going to begin to use the app less.

Please reconsider this change. I’m asking not just for myself, but for so many people who use Snapchat as their main camera roll. We trust the platform to keep our moments safe, and it would mean so much if you kept Memories accessible without charging.

reviews.text:
This app used to be so much fun. I’ve been a user since it’s used to be only pics and one bar to communicate! The app was fun and a great way to visit memory lane.
I remember the first time they tried to charge people $2 for special filters until they gave up and decided to have them available for free. I thought they had learned their lesson with that. Now all this app is, is nothing but ads. There are now filters you have to pay for again. There’s basically a membership you can pay monthly for certain filters and certain features. Honestly paying more for certain features sounds reasonable and fair. It doesn’t take away from the user experience. 
Now where my real issue is laying right now is when I logged in today to look for a certain memory, I saw that the app now wants to charge users for storage. I have been saving pics and videos since 2013! And now I have to pay more to keep them??? It says I have 12 months to move them. I don’t want to pay and I don’t want to have to move them. This is absolutely ridiculous. If that was going to be a feature it should’ve been one from the get-go. Not after saving all of these memories. Now if I do move them, the dates will be all out of order. I could have been saving these photos and videos on iCloud or google photos since I already pay for those. This app is so money hungry it’s actually embarrassing.

reviews.title: Now had to pay for memory storage
reviews.text:
Nearly all of my pictures since 2017 are from Snap Memories.  Suddenly, today, I discovered that you now had to pay for memory storage, and I have a year before all of my memories—which include priceless real-life memories like all of the photos and films (from abroad, etc.)—are erased.  I now need to purchase something to store all of these 5 GB of pictures.

If nothing else, there ought to be a way to download everything at once.  I have no idea how long this will take me to complete.  I'll be deleting Snapchat after a year because, to be honest, I've never really loved it except from memories and filters.  I'm confident that a lot of other people feel the same way and act in the same way.  Since Snapchat was my first social networking app when I was in Australia, I suppose it will live on in my memory (pun intended).

But now it's really frustrating and disappointing.  Is it possible to download images from Snap Memories quickly?  Okay, I get that you're going to remove everything, but at least give us a means to keep and preserve our own pictures.
